chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Nat Cole answers the question about jazz in Denver
summary: A young man asks Cole why he doesn't play jazz and Cole jokes about his beaver cap and tinted glasses.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Another time, Nat King was in Denver, I did a one-nighter, Bill Jones booked

us in and in those days they weren't in the big ball parks but I think it was in the Rainbow, you could hardly move in there, and so the next day we're invited to a dinner, just Nat, the trio and myself were invited. So the young man that invited was a music major at the college there and he fixed up everything and we got to talking and he said to Nat, Mr. Cole, why don't you play some jazz? So Nat said you don't think I play any jazz? So he said, I don't think you do. He said now I like your playing, I was just wondering why you don't play some jazz. He said, well now, to make you know that I'm playing jazz, like everyone else, maybe I didn't have on one of them little beaver pelts and was looking just straight ahead, not looking around at nobody at what's going on or nothing, but I stared and played away and then maybe you would think I'm playing jazz.
So the guy got a laugh and said, well, maybe so. He said I'll tell you what, those different things, even just a little tinted

glasses that made me fall out with my father in law. He said before I married, he said I went to visit my wife--they weren't married-- he was engaged and everything and he told him that he told his daughter that I've seen you before and I just thought you were going wrong, I didn't know if you were hiding and don't want nobody to see your eyes, but you're going around with those dark glasses. So he said he just smiled and said, well, I'm not going to change my glasses, I work in front of lights and these are not really dark glasses, they're just tinted a little so I can see and don't have the glare of the lights.
So he said next time you see me I won't have on no cap and won't be staring, but he said I think I play some jazz.
I think his singing overshadowed his great piano playing.
